clue.text: Nurse once covering right leg

parts.note: a mat is a floor covering
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A former nurse wraps a bandage around a patient's right leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's leg side is also called the on side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior nursing officer of a British hospital was formerly titled this, a role since renamed.

clue.text: Name Nicholas abbreviated during more editing

indicators.note: during means within, so the short name sits inside the rearranged letters
editing reworks the letters of the word more

parts.note: Nick is short for Nicholas

explanation.surface: A name is shortened while being revised further.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a person's name or nickname.

clue.text: Extremely thorough Welshman to tell stories about ancient text

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, the first and last letters, of thorough
about means turned around, so the Welshman and the lie are read backwards

parts.note: Dai is a stock Welsh name
to tell stories is to lie

explanation.surface: A meticulous Welshman spins tales about an old document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses DAILIE to EILIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War is a famous text from antiquity.

clue.text: Old couple extended oriental tea

indicators.note: a couple means two, so the abbreviation for old appears twice

parts.note: extended means long

explanation.surface: An elderly pair linger over an Eastern tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark Chinese tea, partly fermented, so an Eastern variety of tea.

clue.text: Type of bread (includes nuts)

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the word includes go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: A kind of loaf studded with nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like an ingredient in the bracket, but it is the anagram signal working on 'includes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole loaf not yet cut into slices is a common way bread is sold.

clue.text: Child and I leaving native American retreat

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so these letters are taken out of the native American

parts.note: the Chinook are a native American people

explanation.surface: A child and I leave a native American refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A snug sheltered corner is a place to retreat to.

clue.text: Hum with male during weak opera

indicators.note: during means inside, so the smell and the male go within weak

parts.note: a lame excuse is a weak one
a hum is a bad smell, and BO is body odour
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: Humming along with a man during a feeble opera.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a hum is a bad smell, hence BO (body odour).
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera about Parisian bohemians is a famous work of the operatic repertoire.

clue.text: Clergyman attending, has smoke perhaps outside?

indicators.note: outside means the curing word wraps around the attending word

parts.note: smoking is one way to cure fish or meat
at means present at, attending

explanation.surface: A vicar present at an event perhaps nips outside for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant to a parish priest is a junior member of the clergy.

clue.text: Hazel's problem maybe needing doctor to track back

indicators.note: back means the following pieces are read backwards

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Hazel has a medical issue requiring a doctor to retrace steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' looks like a woman's name, but it is the tree, whose timber can rot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungus that decays timber is a problem for wood such as hazel.

clue.text: Require licence to drain sewer?

parts.note: to require something is to need it

indicators.note: draining the word licence empties out its middle, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Asking whether a permit is required to clear a drainage pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' is read not as a drain but as one who sews; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewing tool is something that sews, hence a sewer in the stitching sense.

clue.text: See poet visiting compiler somewhere in Italy

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: visiting means going into, so the poet is placed inside the compiler's word

parts.note: the compiler refers to themselves; my is the setter's possessive
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A sightseer finds a poet calling on the crossword setter somewhere in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The compiler is the setter, giving MY ('my' as the setter's own word).
explanation.definitionFit: A northern Italian region around Milan, so a fair vague pointer to a place in Italy.

clue.text: Go away shortly, vacation in Ibiza, seeing colourful flower

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: begone is an old command to go away

indicators.note: vacating Ibiza empties its middle, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: Leaving quickly on holiday in Ibiza, one sees a bright bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday, but it empties Ibiza to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plant with showy bright blooms is a colourful flowering plant.

clue.text: Article probes rather cool kitchen utensil

indicators.note: an article probing a word goes inside it

parts.note: rather cool means a bit colder
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article investigates a fairly chilly kitchen gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A perforated bowl for draining pasta or vegetables is a standard piece of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Which person assumes headwear for hail?

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on, so the word for which person takes the headwear into it

parts.note: which person asks who
a hat is headwear

explanation.surface: Asking which person dons a hat in order to greet someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned jolly British greeting, used as an interjection like hail or hello.

clue.text: Sweet victory against Spain, cup being lifted

parts.note: a victory is a win
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a mug is a cup

explanation.surface: A sports victory against Spain as the cup is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup' suggests a trophy, but it is a MUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy fruit-flavoured British gum sweet is a type of confectionery.

clue.text: Small space contains advert backing dairy product

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so the small space surrounds the advert

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the advert's letters are reversed

explanation.surface: A small advertising slot promoting a dairy product.
explanation.walkthrough: An em is a printer's spacing unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch cheese with a red wax rind, and cheese is a dairy product.

clue.text: I feel terrible regularly, wrote tipsy writer

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the two words

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themselves as me

explanation.surface: A drunken author complains of feeling awful after writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of 'wrote tipsy' gives WOEIS; the writer is ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An old exclamation of misery or self-pity, said when one feels wretched.

clue.text: Taxi ordered by Geordie non- drinker after one German wine

indicators.note: a taxi is ordered by phone, so the word is said, not spelt

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
I is the Roman numeral for one
a Geordie comes from Newcastle in north-east England, NE
TT means teetotal, a non-drinker

explanation.surface: A cab booked by a teetotal Newcastle man after a drink of German wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the homophone: a phoned order is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A German quality wine category for the lightest, driest grade of fine wine.

clue.text: Stay after ceremonial piece of music

parts.note: to last is to stay or endure
post means after

explanation.surface: Remain behind after a ceremonial musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle call played at military funerals and remembrance services is ceremonial music.

clue.text: Chart written by banks of Kennet on aquatic organisms

parts.note: a plan is a chart or map

indicators.note: banks of the river Kennet are its outside letters

explanation.surface: A map drawn by the banks of the river Kennet on water life.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kennet is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny drifting plants and animals in seas and lakes, collectively aquatic organisms.

clue.text: Perhaps West End's premier gains money for performance

indicators.note: gains means takes in, so money goes inside

parts.note: Mae West, the American actress, is one example of a West
tin is slang for money

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of End is taken

explanation.surface: A West End premiere attracts cash for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London theatreland, but West is Mae West and End supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon showing of a play or film is a kind of theatrical performance.

clue.text: Sort of cup both hands for cake

parts.note: the FA Cup is English football's knockout trophy
R and L stand for right and left hands

explanation.surface: Cupping both hands to hold a piece of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA Cup is England's main football knockout trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish or Irish flat triangular oatcake or griddle bread, loosely a cake.

clue.text: English painter finding stone guest-house in America

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight

indicators.note: in means inside, so the guest-house is put within America

parts.note: US is America
a B&B, bed and breakfast, is a guest-house

explanation.surface: A painter discovers a stone guest-house in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds, ST; a B&B is a bed-and-breakfast guest-house.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs was an 18th-century English artist famed for horse paintings.

clue.text: It's 50:50 one will fit into small boot

indicators.note: will fit into means going inside the small word

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, written twice
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An even chance that a foot will fit a small boot.
explanation.walkthrough: '50:50' looks like odds, but gives two Roman fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial British term for a rubber wellington, a waterproof boot.

clue.text: Keep warm with gunner and dog

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: Staying warm alongside a soldier and his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to dress in warm clothing to stay warm.

clue.text: Repeatedly attach clothing accessory

parts.note: to tie is to attach; repeated, another word for attach is pin
to tie is to attach; repeated, another word for attach is pin

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep fastening on a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' asks for two words for 'attach' in a row, TIE and PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental pin holding a necktie in place is worn as a clothing accessory.

clue.text: After month, seaman's back at home displaying culinary style

indicators.note: after month means the rest follows the month's abbreviation

parts.note: Aug is short for August

indicators.note: back means the seaman's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
in means at home

explanation.surface: After a month away, a sailor home again shows off a cooking style.
explanation.definitionFit: A French cooking term for a dish topped with breadcrumbs or cheese and browned.

clue.text: Disapproving utterance over posh skirt

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so this sound comes first

parts.note: tut is a click of disapproval
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A sniff of disapproval at a fancy skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina's short stiff layered skirt is a kind of skirt.

clue.text: Fine prospect, to act with two lines at theatrical show, runs out

parts.note: to be someone on stage is to act the part
L stands for line, so two lines give LL

indicators.note: out means removed, so the runs letter leaves the show

parts.note: a revue is a theatrical show of sketches and songs
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An actor with two lines in a show sees it close, a fine outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs out' looks like a show closing, but it removes R (runs, in cricket) from REVUE.
explanation.definitionFit: French for beautiful view, and a prospect is a view, so a fine prospect.

clue.text: French novelist, wanting son primarily to develop

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the son's letter is taken from its place
primarily means at the start, so the son's letter goes to the front

parts.note: Marcel Proust was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A French novelist, lacking a son at first, begins to develop.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the S out of PROUST and put it first.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow shoots, as a seed does, is to begin to develop.

clue.text: In periphery of skillet, mushroom turned unusual range of colours

indicators.note: in means the reversed mushroom sits inside the skillet's edges
the periphery of the word skillet is its outside letters
turned means reversed, so the mushroom's letters run backwards

parts.note: a cep is a kind of mushroom
rum is an old word for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A mushroom flipped at the edge of a pan shows an odd range of colours.
explanation.walkthrough: A cep is a porcini mushroom; rum is British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Light split by a prism gives the full band of rainbow hues, a range of colours.

clue.text: Exactly right to use tee when restricted by old golfing club

indicators.note: restricted by means held in, so the tee is enclosed by the club

parts.note: a spoon was an old wooden golf club
tee is the letter T

explanation.surface: Using a tee is correct when an old club restricts it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning precisely accurate, hitting the target exactly.
